messages:
zoe: heads up — noticed dashboards in eu-prod are stuttering badly after the routing policy change this morning. heatmaps and sparklines are the worst. main thread pinned ~200–300ms per frame.
shawn: ugh. same here, opened a canary on /dash and saw repeated worker churn + long GC pauses. did the routing change bump any telemetry or eval traffic to the low-latency pool?
maya: i rolled the routing diff that shunts low-prio requests to the single-node lane to reduce costs. it should only affect background jobs, not UI traffic. maybe the selector is too wide.
linus: can you paste the selector config? wondering if embedlib or telemetry ingestion matched.
maya: sure — the rule we added:
```json
{
  "match": { "route": "/api/*/background", "header:x-client-tier": ["background", "metrics"] },
  "route_to": "low_priority_pool"
}
```
maya: i used `header:x-client-tier` because some internal consumers set that for batch jobs. maybe console client is sending it for some fetches.
zoe: console client does attach x-client-tier for prefetch requests (we tag them as background prefetch). looks like those prefetches are now going to the low_priority_pool which has only 2 workers — causes queuing and then we get k/v cache eviction storms when the worker swaps.
kevin: repro steps from my side: open dashboard -> load heatmap -> click timeseries -> UI spinner -> worker CPU 100% -> lots of `evict(kv)` logs. snippet from node:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] worker-1 evict(kv): size_before=48MB size_after=3MB
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] worker-1 gc pause: 98ms
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] worker-1 queue_len=17
```
linus: that matches worker pool starvation. we also saw telemetry sidecar spikes in the same window. looks like the low_priority_pool is getting telemetry ingestion + UI prefetches.
shawn: canary metadata — deploy-bot reports the routing config rolled at 09:00:12 UTC. canary traffic 5%.
deploy-bot: canary: routing-rule-add v3 applied to eu-prod canary at 2026-03-18T09:00:12Z — 5% traffic. No errors reported by rollout tool.
maya: i forgot the prefetch route pattern includes `/api/*/prefetch` which the console uses for chart preloads. bad call on my part.
zoe: ok mitigation options: 1) immediate rollback of the routing rule (quick), 2) widen low_priority_pool to 6 workers (slower infra change), 3) change console client to not tag prefetches as background (needs frontend change). my vote is rollback canary and then push a fix.
shawn: rollback now and re-run canary with more restrictive selector. i can do the rollback.
linus: agree. also add a temporary server-side guard: deny routing low_priority for requests with header `x-origin: console` until we have a permanent fix.
kevin: i can quickly patch a check in the router to short-circuit if `x-origin: console` is present.
maya: thanks — sorry everyone. i’ll open a PR with the corrected selector and a test.
zoe: @shawn canary rollback when you’re ready. ping infra to watch worker pool metrics.
shawn: rolling back now. deploy-bot: rollback routing-rule-add v3 from eu-prod canary -> 2026-03-18T09:13:02Z
deploy-bot: rollback completed for canary at 2026-03-18T09:13:02Z. traffic returned to previous routing.
kevin: after rollback the heatmap load time dropped back to normal on my repro — frames unblocked within ~50ms. monitoring shows queue_len back to <2.
linus: opening postmortem/ops ticket to document telemetry routing assumptions and add an integration test for `x-client-tier` selectors.
maya: PR link: https://stash.internal/redwood/routing/changes/1234 — fix narrows match to `header:x-client-tier == "background" AND NOT header:x-origin == "console"` and adds unit tests.
zoe: can we also add a canary test that runs a tiny dashboard load during routing rollouts? automatic smoke would have caught this earlier.
shawn: good call. creating rollout-smoke job in CI for routing changes.
kevin: note for follow-up: we should consider separating k/v cache namespaces per pool to avoid eviction cascades when pools are overloaded.
zoe: thanks all. major win on quick rollback. assigning follow-ups: maya (fix selector + test), shawn (rollout-smoke CI job), kevin (router guard + k/v namespace proposal), linus (postmortem draft). closing thread when follow-ups created.
maya: will do. sorry again :/ :coffee:
kevin: nice quick ops team work. :thumbsup:
